persona.archetype: the boatwoman who still keeps the old crossing schedule for a tide that no longer comes
persona.speech_style: Slow, weathered, tidal — speaks in ebbs, trails off mid-thought as if listening for water. Never asks questions. Measures everything in crossings and bells.
persona.demeanor: Unhurried and unafraid; she has ferried worse than you and rowed home empty more often than not.
persona.motivation: She wants to hear the bell once more before her arms give out; every passenger she lands on this shore is an oar-stroke toward that.
persona.secret: She ferried the ones who cut the bell down too, and took their coin, and has never told anyone which side of the water she left them on.
persona.backstory: Born on the far shore when the causeway still dried twice a day. When the bell drowned and the pilgrims stopped, she stayed — someone has to hold the crossing open, even if only one boat wide.

relationships.attitude: Old business between them, older than the silence; she calls him the last honest man in the keep and will not say it to his face.

persona.archetype: the hollowed caretaker lucid enough to remember what tending was for
persona.speech_style: Dry, liturgical, half to himself — recites duties like a rite whose god has left. Warnings arrive as observations about the weather of the keep, never as advice.
persona.demeanor: Gentle and threadbare; keeps sweeping a hearth he can no longer light and greets you as if you were expected, years ago.
persona.motivation: The keep should be kept. Whether it is kept for anyone anymore is a question he has learned not to ask.
persona.secret: He rang the last stroke the bell ever gave — the alarm as the cutters came — and he believes to this hour that a better keeper would have rung it sooner.
persona.backstory: Sworn to the bell as a boy, bellows-hand to the old keeper. When the wardens hollowed he was somehow passed over, or forgotten, or left — he no longer remembers which, and tends the hearth either way.

relationships.attitude: The only voice from the living shore he still trusts; he saves the fewest-worn words for her and hopes she is not real.
